title: Turn Into Picture takes every layer you picked
goal: Pick three shapes, right click one, and Turn Into Picture flattens only the one you clicked while the other two stay shapes. The same is true of Turn Into Path, Separate into Layers and Turn into Text. Everything else in that menu already treats the rows you picked as one thing, so these four should too: the command should run over every picked layer, in one undo step.
notes: Found on 2026-09-13 while adding Group and Ungroup to the layer row menu. Evidence: the row menu in Sources/Photonz/LayersRow.swift calls editorState.rasterizeLayer(id:), turnLayerIntoPath(id:), separateIntoLayers(id:) and turnIntoText(id:), none of which consult multiSelectedLayerIDs, while duplicateLayer(id:), deleteLayer(id:), restack(id:_:), mergeDown(id:), toggleLayerVisibility(id:) and toggleLayerLock(id:) all route through the whole selection when the clicked row is a member. The shared rule is EditorState.rowMenuTargets(_:) in Sources/Photonz/EditorState+Layout.swift; these four just need to read it. Separate into Layers and Turn into Text are only offered on a picture, so batching them matters less than the two Turn Into commands; do those first.
acceptance: With three shapes picked, Turn Into Picture on one of them turns all three into pictures in one undo step
Turn Into Path over a selection does the same, and layers in the selection that have no outline to find are left alone rather than failing the whole command
One undo takes the whole batch back
A row outside the selection still acts on that row alone, which is the rule in docs/design/layers.md
A playtest walk picks two shapes, right clicks one and turns both into pictures

log.note: Turn Into Path is DONE as of 2026-09-15, in 'several-shapes-turn-into-one-path-joined-where-t'. It reads rowMenuTargets now, and over several shapes it does one thing more than a batch: shapes whose ends meet are welded into ONE path (PathJoining.swift), so three lines that meet become a triangle rather than three paths. Layers in the selection with no outline to find are left alone, which is this task's acceptance item 2, and it is one undo step. STILL OUTSTANDING here: Turn Into Picture, Separate into Layers and Turn into Text, which all still act on the clicked row alone. Note for whoever takes those: a batch of Turn Into Picture is N pictures, not one, so it is a plain batch with none of the joining.

Adversarial review before building. (1) Three picked shapes must become THREE pictures, not one: Merge Down already exists for making one thing out of several, and Turn Into Picture's whole promise is that the canvas is identical the instant after and every row keeps its name and slot. A batch that merged would be a destructive command wearing a non-destructive command's name. (2) The question is the part the mock-free version gets wrong: today it names the one layer, 'Turn "Rectangle" into a picture?', and over three that sentence is a lie about which rows are about to change. A batch needs a plural question that says how many and what they lose, the way TurnIntoPathQuestion does. (3) A picture picked alongside two shapes must not stop the command, and must not be counted in the question: same rule Turn Into Path already follows. (4) The marquee refusal pill's 'Turn Into Picture' button is about the ONE layer the marquee hit, so it stays single even when a selection exists; batching it there would change layers the person never aimed at. (5) Separate into Layers is the doubtful one: its result is a canvas pill about ONE picture, a 'what is left in it' memory keyed to ONE bitmap, and a rule about which single piece ends up picked. Batching it needs all three to grow a plural form, which is a bigger and more arguable change than the command earns. Turn into Text has none of that trouble: one picture in, one text layer out.

Built and verified as far as a locked screen allows. Turn Into Picture now reads rowMenuTargets from the row menu (EditorState.rasterizeLayer(id:)) and actionableLayerIDs from the Layer menu (new rasterizeSelection()/canRasterizeSelection), and applyRasterize bakes every shape and piece of text in the pick and writes them all in ONE perform, so one undo takes the batch. New core: PhotonzDocument.rasterizableLayers(ids:) picks what will really turn, bottom of the stack first, skipping pictures, groups and measurements; RasterizeQuestion is the plural question ('Turn both shapes into pictures?', 'Turn all 3 layers into pictures?', what each kind loses, and that one undo puts them all back), with one layer still asking the singular RasterizePrompt word for word. Twelve new tests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/RasterizeBatchTests.swift; the whole suite is green at 7686 tests. The marquee refusal pill's button deliberately stays single (rasterizeLayers(ids: [id])): the pill named one layer, so the button may not change others.
